transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I came in because... well, I keep hearing voices. It's as clear as if somebody is standing right there in my little studio apartment with me. They keep saying my name, and they tell me that my work is being judged. And... it happens even when the house is completely quiet and I know nobody else is there.
How long have you been hearing these voices—when did they first start?
Well, it's been about nine months now. That's when I first started hearing them... and when I started getting this fixed fear that everything I do at work is being watched.
During these past nine months, have you also noticed periods where your mood was very low, hopeless, or unusually elevated or irritable, lasting for days or weeks at a time?

Yes, I have noticed that. It's... well, sometimes I get this feeling where I am just so bright and chosen. Like I have all these big plans, and the whole town of Greenville just isn't big enough to hold them all. 

But then... I can go right from feeling that way to just snapping hard at someone over the smallest little thing. Like at work, if one of my clients just asks me to repeat myself, I'll just snap at them. It's like I have no patience all of a sudden. So yes, my mood definitely goes up and down like that.
During times when your mood feels normal or stable—not unusually high or irritable—do you still hear the voices or have the feeling that your work is being watched?

Yes, they actually do. Um, I remember a time not too long ago... right after all that high energy finally dropped off. I was sleeping more normally again, and my mood felt pretty level. 

But even then, the voices didn't stop. They kept right on going for several weeks, and I still had that same strong belief that people were tracking and judging everything I did at work. So, yeah, it happens even when I'm feeling completely normal otherwise.

Over the full nine months since this all started, would you say your mood swings—the high energy periods and the irritability—have been happening most of the time, or have they been relatively brief compared to how long the voices and the feeling of being watched have been going on?

Well, if I look back at the whole nine months... I'd say the mood swings have been happening most of the time. For most of this stretch, I was either completely wound up—you know, with all those big plans, getting barely any sleep, and just moving nonstop—or I was coming down from that, but still not feeling quite back to myself. So, yeah, those mood changes have been there for the majority of the time.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has experienced persistent auditory hallucinations (hearing her name called) and persecutory/referential delusions (belief that her work is being watched and judged) for 9 months. Concurrently, she has had manic-like symptoms (elevated/grandiose mood, decreased need for sleep, irritability, racing plans) that have been present for the majority of the illness duration, satisfying the mood episode component. Critically, she reported a period of several weeks where her mood was stable/euthymic but the hallucinations and delusions persisted, confirming that psychotic symptoms occur independently of mood episodes for a significant period (>2 weeks), which is the key distinguishing feature from a mood disorder with psychotic features. The concurrent presence of both mood episode and psychotic symptoms for most of the illness course, combined with psychosis persisting in the absence of mood symptoms, supports a diagnosis of schizoaffective disorder rather than bipolar disorder with psychotic features (F30.2) or schizophrenia (F20.9). Bipolar and depressive type could not be further specified from available history, supporting the unspecified code.
